title: Car Fleets
statement:
Cars drive toward a finish line on a single lane where nobody can pass; count the groups that arrive together.

Contract
- `target` is the position of the finish line. `positions[i]` is where car `i` starts (all distinct, `0 <= positions[i] < target`) and `speeds[i]` is its constant speed (`> 0`). The arrays have equal length and may be empty.
- All cars drive toward `target`. A car cannot overtake: if it catches a slower car ahead it joins it and from then on moves at that slower car's speed.
- A fleet is a set of cars that reach `target` at the same moment, including cars that merge exactly at the line. A lone car is a fleet of one.
- Return the number of fleets. `positions` is not sorted. Do not mutate either array. Compare arrival times exactly (no floating-point rounding errors).

Examples
- `countFleets(100, new int[]{10, 40, 70}, new int[]{5, 3, 1})` returns `1`: the car at 70 is slowest and the cars behind it pile up behind it.
- `countFleets(50, new int[]{0, 10, 20}, new int[]{1, 2, 4})` returns `3`: every car ahead is faster, so nobody catches up.
- `countFleets(12, new int[]{3}, new int[]{2})` returns `1`.
hints: Each car on its own would arrive after (target - position) / speed time units. Think about which cars could ever interfere with each other.
Process cars from the one closest to the line backwards. A car whose solo arrival is no later than the fleet directly ahead catches it and joins that fleet; a later arrival starts a new fleet.

Sort by position (keep each speed with its position), sweep from the front and track the arrival time of the fleet ahead, comparing times with cross-multiplication in long arithmetic. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time for the sort and O(n) space for the sorted pairs, where n is the number of cars.
inputSyntax: Input: the target, then the positions, then the speeds, for example: 100 [10, 40, 70] [5, 3, 1]
